subject: SEV-2: Tokenization service intermittent 502s — customer update & remediation plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: OptiHealth Support <support@optihealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: [SEV-2] Intermittent 502s seen in tokenization service (initial detection)

Team / OptiHealth,

We're seeing intermittent 502 errors originating from the tokenization microservice in us-west-2 starting ~09:05 PT. Error rate spiked to ~7% of requests to /v1/tokenize for a 20-minute window, then fell; we've observed two smaller recurrences since. Impact appears to be increased client-side retries and 5xx responses for some streaming calls.

What we've done so far:
- Rolled a 10% traffic diversion to stable replica (in progress).
- Restarted the affected service instances on the suspect host pool.
- Captured heap/thread dumps and request traces (attached: incident_snapshot_1116.log).
- Opened Jira OPS-11762 and flagged as SEV-2.

Immediate ask for OptiHealth: can you confirm whether your ingestion pipeline saw elevated client errors in the 09:00–09:30 PT window and whether retries were observable? This will help scope customer impact.

We will stand up a short bridge and follow with an executive-facing summary once we have mitigation and timeline.

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: incident_snapshot_1116.log (7.2 KB)
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@optihealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Trevor Morales <trevor@optihealth.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 09:20:18 -0800
Subject: Re: [SEV-2] Intermittent 502s seen in tokenization service (initial detection)

Thanks Ben — we saw a spike of 502s during the period you mentioned. Our front-end reported an uptick in failed requests which triggered some alerting and a few user-visible retries; we also saw delayed background jobs (batch tokenization) queueing up. No data loss observed, but latency and retry counts rose.

We appreciate the quick response — we'll be on the bridge.

— Sarah
Sarah Nguyen
Head of Platform Engineering
OptiHealth

Ben / Michael, take ownership of telemetry and log correlation. Naomi, please prepare a brief executive note for OptiHealth summarizing impact and credit options we may offer.

For OptiHealth: attached is our tokenization runbook (runbook_tokenization_v2.pdf) — it documents common mitigation steps (service diversion, instance restarts, config rollbacks) and customer-visible fallback options. We'll share an executive summary after the first mitigation step completes.

Agenda for 10:00 PT bridge:

- 10:10 — Mitigation steps attempted and immediate telemetry (Karthik)
- 10:20 — Customer impact assessment / communications (Laura / Naomi)
- 10:30 — Proposed next actions & timeline

If OptiHealth prefers a separate exec-only briefing, we can schedule that at 11:30 PT.

Laura Bennett

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: OptiHealth — Sarah Nguyen <sarah@optihealth.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 12:45:22 -08:00
Subject: [Update] Bridge notes and remediation plan (tokenization)

Quick update from the bridge:
- Root cause (preliminary): a memory leak in a dependency introduced in the 2027-11-10 tokenization release that under load causes request handlers to stall and return 502s. Repro steps captured in OPS-11762.
- Short-term action: divert 80% traffic to stable replica (completed 11:20 PT) and increased instance pool size for the replica set to absorb burst. Error rate dropped to ~0.4% for affected endpoints.
- Medium-term action: rollback the 2027-11-10 release in us-west-2 to remove the offending binary; scheduled for 02:00 PT (11/17) to minimize customer impact.
- Customer-visible mitigations: enable the streaming fallback flag for OptiHealth queries (non-disruptive) — Laura, Naomi: please confirm if OptiHealth wants us to opt them in now or after the rollback window.

Telemetry notes: attached traces and the incident snapshot show the stall pattern. We will run additional soak tests post-rollback.

Karthik Iyer
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: OptiHealth — Sarah Nguyen <sarah@optihealth.com>, OptiHealth — Trevor Morales <trevor@optihealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2027 15:05:03 -08:00
Subject: Executive summary & next steps — Tokenization service intermittent 502s (Post-bridge update)

Sarah / Trevor — thank you again for the patience and collaboration on this. Below is a concise executive summary and our commitments following the SEV-2 event.

What happened (brief):
- On 2027-11-16 starting ~09:05 PT, some requests to our tokenization API experienced intermittent 502s caused by a memory leak in a dependency introduced in a Nov 10 release. The issue increased client retries and latency for a subset of traffic in us-west-2.

Impact:
- Transient user-facing retries and delayed background batch jobs for OptiHealth during the elevated window. No data loss reported. Estimated affected request volume: ~2.4% of your tokenization throughput during peak impact window.

What we did:
- Activated traffic diversion to stable replica sets and increased capacity to reduce error surface.
- Collected diagnostic artifacts and traces (see attached).
- Scheduled a rollback of the Nov 10 release in us-west-2 to 02:00 PT on 2027-11-17; rollback completed and soak tests passed.
- Offered streaming-fallback flag as a temporary customer-side mitigation.

Current status:
- Service is back to normal in us-west-2 following the rollback and soak testing. Error rates have returned to baseline.

Our commitments and next steps:
- We will provide a postmortem with a root-cause analysis and action plan within 72 hours (draft attached: postmortem_draft_v0.1.pdf).
- Short-term: we'll add an automatic canary rollback for the tokenization release workflow to reduce blast radius for similar regressions.
- Medium-term: dependency vetting steps will be added to the pre-release CI to catch the leak earlier.
- Customer relief: we are prepared to discuss a service credit for the incident window; Naomi will follow up with options.

If you'd like a live exec briefing, we can schedule a 20-minute call this week. Otherwise, we'll send the finalized postmortem and recommended changelog items.

Apologies for the disruption — we take availability seriously and appreciate the partnership.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Head of Account Success (Strategic)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: postmortem_draft_v0.1.pdf (12 KB)
